sections.heading: 1. The heel check
lines: ① Sit on the seat, pedal at the lowest point.
② Put your heel on the pedal: leg just straight.
③ Pedal on the ball of the foot: slight bend.
④ Adjust a few mm at a time, ride a few days.

sections.heading: 2. Stop and get checked if…
lines: Knee pain gets worse, or your hands
or saddle area go numb — stop and ask.

caption:
Mr Turtle has started riding to work in the CBD, but the front of his knee aches the more he pedals.

A seat that is too low means the knee bends a lot with every stroke, which can load the front of the knee. Too high, and the hips can rock side to side. A common starting point is a slight knee bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.

Hybi's 1-minute check: heel on the pedal at the bottom, leg just straight. Adjust a few millimetres at a time.

Swelling, numbness, or no change after two weeks is worth an assessment. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can help. Book online via the link in bio
